record.original_question: Further develop the theory of program-size complexity for infinite computations, with particular attention to the relationship between program-size complexity and algorithmic probability.

evidence.quote: Further develop the theory of program-size complexity for infinite computations. Particularly, study the relations between program-size complexity and algorithmic probability. (G. J. Chaitin)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a universal Turing machine $U$ that is allowed to run forever, producing a (possibly infinite) output. For a (possibly infinite) binary string $x$, define the program-size complexity for infinite computations as
$$H_\infty(x) \;=\; \min\{\,|p|\ :\ U\text{ on input }p\text{ eventually outputs every finite prefix of }x\,\},$$
and define the algorithmic probability for infinite computations as
$$P_\infty(x) \;=\; \sum_{p:\ U(p)\text{ produces }x} 2^{-|p|},$$
where the programs $p$ are drawn from a prefix-free (self-delimiting) domain and "$U(p)$ produces $x$" means that the (possibly nonterminating) computation of $U$ on $p$ outputs all finite prefixes of $x$.

Develop a systematic theory of $H_\infty$ for infinite (nonterminating) computations of self-delimiting universal machines, and in particular establish the precise quantitative relationship between $H_\infty(x)$ and $-\log_2 P_\infty(x)$ for arbitrary (finite or infinite) binary objects $x$. Determine whether the coding-theorem-style identity
$$H_\infty(x) \;=\; -\log_2 P_\infty(x) \;+\; O(1)$$
holds in this setting, or otherwise characterize the discrepancy between these two quantities.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed by G. J. Chaitin as part of a list of open problems in algorithmic information theory, asks for further development of program-size complexity for infinite computations and its relationship with algorithmic probability. There has been work by Becher, Chaitin, Grigorieff and others on AIT for non-halting computations, but no general coding-theorem-style equivalence in this setting appears to have been definitively established; the problem is generally regarded as still open.
